coupling: The clip commit only widens the unclipped column-walk predicate from `< width` to `<= width` on the endpoint that can land on the exclusive right edge. cell_add() still returns when `(unsigned) col >= width`, so that extra column is dropped and this diff alone never stores past the width-sized row accumulators. The widen commit only replaces those unclipped cell_add() calls with cell_add_fast(), which does the same area/cover update with no range check. Under the predicate those calls had in the original commit (`< width`) every index is in range, and in-range results match cell_add(), so this diff alone is not a memory error either. The heap overflow exists only in the composition: a draw whose edge endpoint column equals the surface width is admitted to the fast path and cell_add_fast() writes one past the buffers allocated by resize_dirty(ext.width). Neither diff contains a local defect to repair on its own. Keeping the inclusive predicate the clip commit introduced and keeping the branch-free update the widen commit introduced are each consistent with that commit, and either half left as introduced still combines with the other half to store column `width`. A correct fix has to reconcile the admission predicate with the unchecked store, which cannot be decided from either diff alone; patching only one commit's diff while leaving the other commit's change in place leaves the out-of-bounds write reachable.
